newsitem.title: MEXICO: MEXICO SAYS STATES WORRIED OVER LOWER VAT PROPOSAL.
newsitem.headline: MEXICO SAYS STATES WORRIED OVER LOWER VAT PROPOSAL.

text.p: Mexico's state treasurers are worried about recent proposals to alter the country's tax system, especially reducing value added tax (VAT), the Tax Administration System (SAT) said Sunday.
In a statement, the quasi-independent unit of the Finance Ministry said the country's 32 state treasurers called on legislators to carry out careful analyses before voting to modify the tax system.

Mexican opposition parties want to lower the VAT from its current 15 percent. The ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) lost its absolute majority and a key element of its 68-year grip on power in the lower house of Congress in July 6 elections. Congressional proposals to reduce the VAT are expected in the second half of the year.

SAT said the call by the state treasurers was made irrespective of party allegiances and came after a meeting with Tomas Ruiz, the president of SAT, which has replaced the Finance Ministry's revenues department.

"They pointed out that any eventual lowering of the VAT would have an impact on state and municipal funds to the tune of 1.26 billion pesos for every percentage point reduced and 6.3 billion pesos in the case of a drastic reduction to 10 percent from 15 percent in the tax rate," SAT said.
SAT added that VAT revenues so far this year have represented 25 percent of federal revenues.
